judgment.rationale: Same statement-type grain (both Indicators). B1.2.1.1.1 'Handle books appropriately' (BASIC 1, rank 0; Strand 2: Reading, Sub-Strand 1: Pre-Reading Activities, under B1.2.1.1 'Know how a text works for reading and writing') is an emergent print-concepts/book-handling behaviour. B2.6.1.1.1 'Read a variety of age and level-appropriate books and texts from print and non-print' (BASIC 2, rank 1; Strand 6: Extensive Reading, Sub-Strand 1: Building the Love and Culture of Reading, under B2.6.1.1 'Read widely for pleasure and to demonstrate independent reading and learning in the literary area') is about sustained independent engagement with varied texts. The two are substantively coherent and mutually reinforcing within early reading instruction: knowing how to handle and orient to books complements building a habit of reading varied print and non-print materials, so this is more than generic repetition of the token 'books'. But the evidence shows no substantive extension, deepening, or combination of the BASIC 1 capability in the BASIC 2 indicator — wide independent reading depends on decoding, fluency and comprehension capabilities that are not evidenced as growth from book handling, and the endpoints sit in different strands and sub-strands. Nomination support is limited to one shared LC/SFI token ('books'), a shared LC tag ('reading'), 'appropriate'/'books' trigram overlap, and weak local rank proximity, which permit direction but do not license a developmental claim. Symmetric relatesTo with null direction is therefore the supported judgment. Evidence depth is limited: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge/code context (including case-duplicate grade merges), which does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 2 Content Standards under Strand 2: Reading (same statement-type grain, same coordinate rank 1), but in distinct Sub-Strands: B2.2.9.1 'Read texts fluently' (Sub-Strand 9: Fluency) and B2.2.7.2 'Use knowledge skills and techniques of reading to understand and interpret texts' (Sub-Strand 7: Comprehension). The fluency source context shows the indicator focus on reading texts/stories/passages 'with good pace, accuracy and expression', i.e. accurate automatic oral reading, while the comprehension standard requires applying reading skills and techniques to understand and interpret text meaning (source context references purpose and features of information texts). Within this same-grade pairing the substantive change is from executing accurate, well-paced reading of text to extracting and interpreting meaning from it; proficiency in fluent reading plausibly supports success in understanding and interpreting the same texts, supporting a same-rank developmental direction from the fluency standard to the comprehension standard rather than the reverse. Evidence limitation: nomination signals (shared BASIC 2 grade/Strand ancestry, adjacent source pages, weak code-prefix and low token/trigram overlap on 'texts'/'read') are not themselves semantic, both endpoints have no Learning Components supplied and truncated source evidence, so the judgment rests on the visible statement text and sub-strand placement.

B3.4.9.1.1 (Sub-Strand 9: Writing as a Process, under B3.4.9.1 'Apply the skills and strategies for idea generation, selection, development, organization and revision in writing') teaches prewriting: select a topic on familiar themes, brainstorm and organise ideas before writing, with LCs 'Select a topic on familiar themes', 'Brainstorm ideas before writing', 'Organise ideas before writing'. B3.3.13.1.1 (Sub-Strand 13: Persuasive/Argumentative Writing, under 'Support an opinion in writing') requires composing a short paragraph supporting an opinion or claim with clear reasons, and its bounded source-context label shows the exemplar 'Choose a simple topic for an argument', i.e. the same topic-selection/idea-organisation moves applied to an argumentative product. Proficiency in generating, selecting and organising ideas before writing plausibly supports success in producing an organised, reason-supported opinion paragraph; the reverse is not supported. The shared 'writing' tag and Strand/Grade ancestry alone were not treated as sufficient; the pair-specific prewriting-to-composition link is the basis. Confidence is moderate because the link is an enabling process skill applied to a genre task rather than an explicit curricular sequence, and both endpoints' source evidence excerpts are truncated.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content Standards in BASIC 3 (rank 2), Strand 4: Writing, so grain and grade scope match. B3.4.3.1 (Sub-Strand 3: Writing/Copying Letters - Small and Capital) targets letter-level production: using skills, strategies and letter-sound knowledge to write letters legibly and boldly. B3.4.5.1 (Sub-Strand 5: Writing Simple Words and Sentences) targets accurate composition of words and sentences using acquired vocabulary and knowledge of grammar (continuation source text: 'using word recognition and knowledge of grammar and vocabulary'). The substantive change is unit of production and control: reliable letter formation and letter-sound representation is the enabling sub-skill for accurately encoding words and sentences, so proficiency in the letter-level standard supports success in the word/sentence-level standard. Direction at equal rank rests on this letter-to-word/sentence capability expansion, not on shared Strand, adjacent codes, page proximity, or generic shared tokens ('write', 'knowledge', 'and', 'of'), which alone would not justify an edge. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 and 35 omitted source evidence items), no Learning Components are supplied, and the second endpoint is an upstream merge of a CONT'D occurrence with slightly differing wording, so the judgment rests on the bounded statement text and hierarchy only.
